note: He passes on starting point and fails on economics. Not deconditioned in any sense — a regular gym-goer who walks a thousand feet of incline in half an hour, has run four extended fasts and took himself from 245 lb to 190 lb unaided — and squarely good-to-great: at 210 lb he wants to be lean, do ten pull-ups and be capable, not rescued. Health is genuinely the deferred corner after thirteen and a half years of, in his words, doing everything for the family. The two economic criteria both fail on evidence. He is a business owner only in the newest sense — 'it's a small business, I just started it, I don't have employees, I'm just running this little thing on my own... it's kind of keeping the lights on, I haven't built it up yet' — and income fails outright: six thousand in the bank earmarked for bills and rent, more owing on the credit card than in the account, a house to sell and condo deposits to find in the middle of a divorce. This is the third call in this batch where the stated ICP's income criterion is the one that fails and the payment structure is reshaped until the deal fits anyway, which is exactly the pattern the ICP file's third observation predicts — except here the reshaping went as far as inventing a one-month tier and putting it on a credit card.
